title: Asking the way when lost
setting: You came out of the wrong station exit. Your phone is at 4%. There's a woman waiting at a crossing.

n1.speaker: narration
n1.english: You need to open the conversation. How?

options.feedback: Always open with すみません. It signals 'I'm about to ask you something' and gives the other person a beat to turn toward you.
Greeting a stranger on the street with こんにちは before a request is a little odd — it reads as social rather than practical. すみません is the tool for this.
ちょっと to get a stranger's attention is brusque, and can read as a complaint incoming. Anime uses it freely between characters who already know each other.
States the problem before the question. People respond to this very warmly in Japan.
Direct and effective, especially with a map held out.
Smart opener — it makes the other person slow down before they've said anything complicated.

n3.speaker: passerby
n3.japanese: どちらへ行きたいんですか。
n3.romaji: Dochira e ikitai n desu ka.
n3.english: Where do you want to go?
n3.audioHint: どちらへいきたいんですか

options.japanese: この住所に行きたいです。
options.english: I want to go to this address. (showing phone)
options.feedback: Showing beats pronouncing. Address readings are genuinely hard even for Japanese speakers.
If you just need a landmark to reorient from, this is the faster question.

n4.speaker: passerby
n4.japanese: ああ、それなら次の信号を右に曲がって、まっすぐ行くと左側にありますよ。歩いて五分ぐらいです。
n4.romaji: Ā, sore nara tsugi no shingō o migi ni magatte, massugu iku to hidarigawa ni arimasu yo. Aruite gofun gurai desu.
n4.english: Ah, in that case turn right at the next light, go straight, and it's on the left. About five minutes on foot.
n4.audioHint: ああ、それならつぎのしんごうをみぎにまがって、まっすぐいくとひだりがわにありますよ。あるいてごふんぐらいです

options.feedback: The right call — that was fast and dense. Asking for it slower gets you the whole thing again, not a shortened version.
Even better. A spoken route evaporates; a finger on a map doesn't.
Be careful with わかりました here. Saying you understood when you caught maybe half of it ends the conversation and leaves you no better off — this is the most common politeness trap for learners.

n5.speaker: passerby
n5.japanese: ここです。この道をまっすぐ。すぐ分かりますよ。
n5.romaji: Koko desu. Kono michi o massugu. Sugu wakarimasu yo.
n5.english: It's here. Straight along this road. You'll spot it easily.
n5.audioHint: ここです。このみちをまっすぐ。すぐわかりますよ

options.feedback: Done. A small bow along with it is natural and costs nothing.
Past form, because the help is complete. Both work here.
'You're welcome' — but they helped you. Under pressure it's easy to grab the wrong half of a thanks/reply pair.

end.speaker: narration
end.english: Back on course. The real skill in this scenario isn't asking — it's admitting you didn't catch the answer. ゆっくりお願いします is worth more than any vocabulary here.
